prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Asset type: finished 16:9 landscape background for an original Chinese cultivation RPG city interior overview, approximately 1672x941, opaque, WITHOUT any UI or text.
Primary request: redesign Baishi immortal city. Learn the clear functional-building hierarchy and walkable spaces of the third reference (Mi Chang Sheng city screenshot), but render the entire new original city in the exact muted palette and matte gouache/watercolor visual language of the first two references (the project's actually installed Yuxu sect). This is a full new composition, not a color filter on the old dense roof map.

Reference roles: Image 1 is the authoritative COLOR AND PAINTING reference: blue-grey roof planes, pale grey stone, restrained ochre timber, olive-grey green trees, cool desaturated atmospheric stone and cream. Image 2 is authoritative for broad matte painted surfaces and architectural construction. Image 3 only explains hierarchy: a few clearly recognizable important buildings linked by generous walkable streets and plazas. Do not copy its architecture or arrangement. Do not reproduce its walls, portal, glowing circles, labels, people or HUD. Do not borrow its saturated teal, black linework or flat cartoon look.

Composition: a high oblique bird's-eye view, around 55 degrees downward, of a PORTION of a vast prosperous IMMORTAL CITY. The city continues past the left, right and lower edges, with more large roofs and distant roof bands beyond the visible neighborhoods. Do not show a bounded whole settlement. No city perimeter walls, fortifications, gate towers, enclosing square city boundary or miniature walled-city diorama. All four corners are fully painted, sharp and clear, no blurry vignette and no faded white edges. Sky and distant blue-grey foothills occupy at most the upper 12% of the image. City ground and architecture dominate.

Four connected neighborhoods, not four detached islands or four identical courtyard blocks:
1. North-center, around x=0.50 y=0.28: imposing city administration compound, tall multi-storey eaved hall with subordinate buildings, its broad forecourt and side lecture courtyard are part of the same built fabric. The front street at x=0.50 y=0.36 is visibly connected to both the main city hall entrance and neighboring lanes. No special free-standing ritual monument.
2. Right-middle, around x=0.72 y=0.55: commercial quarter with distinctive tall multi-storey merchant houses, varied roof silhouettes, an open stone-paved market space and connected shop-front streets. Do not make it a grid of tiny repeated houses.
3. Lower-center-left, around x=0.45 y=0.73: the main southern street, a generous natural bend or diagonal connection, recognizable large inn and roadside commercial architecture, with cropped foreground roofs continuing out of frame. Not a grand perfectly straight mirror-symmetrical imperial boulevard.
4. Left-middle, around x=0.28 y=0.46: older interconnected lanes, layered large courtyard residences and mature trees; narrow streets actually join the wider market and north streets. Ordinary housing is supporting context, not most of the picture.

Learn from the Mi Chang Sheng screenshot that important places need readable silhouettes and open approach space: each neighborhood has one or two major recognizable anchors, with smaller buildings subordinate. Give the city grand immortal architecture, tall halls, layered roofs, stone terraces and varied commercial buildings; it must not feel like a village, a generic residential housing map or a copied royal palace. Group roof masses instead of drawing hundreds of individual tiny tiles and equal-size courtyards. Show scale through overlapping and off-frame roof bands, not an exact countable closed city. Streets, stone steps and courtyard doors must physically connect. Stairs land on actual ground, roofs have coherent supports, no impossible bridges or dangling connectors.

Style and palette: exactly the desaturated blue-grey / ivory-grey / muted olive / restrained ochre relationships of reference 1 and 2. Broad clean matte pigment shapes, quiet hand-painted edge variation, subtle paper character, architectural shadows in muted grey-blue. Keep natural daytime light like Yuxu. Gold is a tiny trim accent only. Avoid yellow parchment wash, orange-red city grading, vivid green, black outlines, photorealism, glossy 3D, hyper-detailed roof etching, dense white dots or gold flecks on leaves and masonry, glitter, stippling, bloom and extreme haze. Do not fill streets with cloud banks.

Interface integration: important landmarks and approach spaces predominantly inside x=0.25..0.78 and y=0.18..0.78. Side edges still have believable continuous city fabric, no artificial blank UI boxes. Future labels will be separate game controls, so paint no signs, labels, plaques with letters, words, calligraphy, numbers, icons or watermark. No people, animals, player pawns, HUD or decorative interface frames.
